memoryText: And whatever you do, in word or deed, do everything in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God the Father through him.
readingInstruction: No new reading today. Read Colossians 3:17 slowly, several times, and try to say it from memory. Then read the meditation and the week in review, and choose one of the three questions to write about, pray over, or share with someone.
memoryVerseMeditation:
This verse is a summary of a whole way of life.

“And whatever you do.” The scope is total. Not just the religious parts of life, but everything. Eating, working, speaking, parenting, driving, resting.

“In word or deed.” Our speech and our actions both. Together they make up the whole of what we show the world.

“Do everything in the name of the Lord Jesus.” To act in someone’s name is to act on his authority and on his behalf. A Christian is an ambassador. We represent Christ in every place. We ask: Would he put his name on this? Does this honor him?

“Giving thanks to God the Father through him.” The attitude is gratitude. Everything we have comes from the Father through the Son. Thanksgiving turns ordinary tasks into worship.

This verse removes the divide between sacred and secular. A meal can be a prayer, a job can be worship, a conversation can be ministry.

When your day feels ordinary or scattered, say this verse. Offer it all in his name, with thanks.
weekInReview: This week you finished Colossians and read 1 Thessalonians. Colossians 2 and 3 warned against empty philosophy and human tradition and taught that the old covenant regulations were a shadow whose substance is Christ. Because we have been raised with Christ, we seek the things above, put off the old self, put on compassion, kindness, humility, and love, and let the word of Christ dwell in us richly. Chapter 3 and 4 applied this to households, work, prayer, and speech. A doctrinal pause considered ordinary work as service to the Lord Christ. First Thessalonians presented a model church that turned from idols to serve the living God and wait for his Son, a pastor’s tender heart, comfort for those who grieve, and a series of final commands: rejoice always, pray without ceasing, give thanks in all circumstances. A doctrinal pause on the return of Christ affirmed that he will come again to raise the dead and gather his people.
reflectionQuestions: Colossians 3:23 says to work heartily, as for the Lord and not for men. What task in your week do you do half-heartedly? How might you do it differently if you remembered who your real Master is?
Paul told the Thessalonians not to grieve as those who have no hope. Who is someone you could comfort with the hope of Christ’s return and the resurrection? What will you say or do?
First Thessalonians 5:16-18 gives three short commands: rejoice, pray, give thanks. Which is hardest for you right now? What might help you practice it?
prayerPrompts: Offer what you do this week to God, giving thanks to the Father through Jesus.
Thank him that Christ is coming.
